newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche - no concrete plans to cut stakes.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche - no concrete plans to cut stakes.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG, holding its annual shareholders' meeting, said on Tuesday it had no concrete plans at present to reduce its industrial shareholdings in Germany.

Asked if the bank planned to reduce its shareholdings, a spokesman said: "No, we reduce our holdings here or there by not participating in capital raisings but there are no concrete plans to change the ownership of shareholdings."

Deutsche's new chief executive, Rolf Breuer, was quoted in a newspaper interview on Tuesday as saying he plans to reduce the bank's industrial holdings in German companies in a bid to achieve a balance between its domestic and international holdings.

Breuer, who takes over as chief executive after Deutsche's annual shareholder meeting on Tuesday, was quoted in the Financial Times as saying there could eventually be a 50-50 balance between holdings in German companies and those held abroad.
But he added this would probably not happen until the next century and depended on how quickly taxes would be cut.
Deutsche's holdings in German industrial companies include a 22.6 percent stake in Daimler-Benz AG and 10 percent in insurer Allianz AG Holding AG.
Its stakes also include 25.8 percent of Philip Holzmann AG, Deutz AG, 10 percent of Munich Reinsurance and 10.2 percent of Continental AG.
Breuer also said that international diversification of its holdings would provide more shareholder value for investors, the paper said.
